subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` with a DeepSeek auto-default, or keep the cache workaround provider-internal/config-free?
rationale: Repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces, and two open PRs propose materially different permanent provider contracts; automation cannot choose that public API direction.

options.title: Approve the scoped compat contract
options.body: Keep the public option, auto-enable it only for DeepSeek, retain explicit `false` rollback and Xiaomi opt-in, then require the sanitization fix and exact-head proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the policy provider-internal
options.body: Remove the public compat surface and implement only a DeepSeek-owned default if custom-provider opt-in is not worth a durable configuration contract.

options.title: Prefer the config-free sibling
options.body: Pause this PR and require the sibling strategy to repair its transport path and provide positive live proof before it becomes canonical.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped compat contract
recommendation.body: Keep the public option, auto-enable it only for DeepSeek, retain explicit `false` rollback and Xiaomi opt-in, then require the sanitization fix and exact-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history connects this person to DeepSeek provider behavior, prompt-cache boundaries, and the compatibility types whose long-term contract needs selection.
